findings.mitigation: File D-036 in docs/DECISIONS.md before merge: 'Adopt policies/VERSIONING.md MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH semver contract with one-release deprecation ramp AND docs/reviews/rule-proposals/ RFC-lite process (quorum=1 per D-031 single-operator mode, 48h wall-clock, auto-defer on zero approvals, closure of BS-5) as estate doctrine for SCP federation primitive versioning and rule governance. Closes WP-SCP-020 §4 020H.1 (i)+(ii)+(iii). Rationale: parallel to D-035 — every new governance procedure binding adopters ships a ratifying D-NNN for durable decision traceability.' Add a STATUS.md 'Recent decisions' row for D-036 (2026-05-01).

findings.claim: Plan sub-criterion (iv-b) specifies 'SCP-side canary re-run on each release (CI matrix across all three canaries)' but canary-replay.yml delivers weekly Monday cron + workflow_dispatch only — no on:release trigger. DISPATCH-NOTE conflates (iv-b) with (iv-d) without acknowledging the spec gap.
findings.evidence: Plan §4 020H.1 sub-criterion (iv-b): 'SCP-side canary re-run on each release (CI matrix across all three canaries).' canary-replay.yml on: block contains only 'schedule: - cron: "0 9 * * MON"' and 'workflow_dispatch' — no 'release' event. DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance item (iv-b): 'existing scripts/replay-canary.sh (landed in 020E.c) covers this; the new cron (iv-d) automates it on a schedule.' This treats the weekly cron as closing (iv-b) rather than acknowledging that a release cut Tuesday–Sunday would not automatically trigger canary replay.
findings.impact: A regression introduced in a mid-week release would not be automatically detected until the following Monday (up to 6 days). Manual workflow_dispatch provides a workaround but is not automatic. The plan's 'on each release' spec is not met. The 'best-effort rollback detection' posture partially absorbs this, but DISPATCH-NOTE closure of (iv-b) against a weekly-only delivery without acknowledgement of the delta is incomplete.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) add an 'on: release: types: [published]' trigger to canary-replay.yml (preferred — closes the spec gap exactly and does not require a new TF item); or (b) document the delta explicitly: add a sentence to the DISPATCH-NOTE acknowledging '(iv-b) is partially satisfied — replay-canary.sh exists and the weekly cron provides regular detection; on-each-release automation is forward-compat, filed as TF-020H1-NNN.' Do not claim (iv-b) closed against a delivery that omits the release-event trigger.

findings.claim: ADOPT-001 §12.7.5 step 4 retains the forward-looking parenthetical '(lands in 020H.1)' which becomes stale historical text at merge time. The DISPATCH-NOTE claims the §12.7.5 forward-looking flag as closed but does not update the text.
findings.evidence: ADOPT-001 §12.7.5 step 4: 'Open an issue at https://github.com/jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/issues using the `rule-regression` template (lands in 020H.1) so SCP-side detection workflows correlate.' The parenthetical is accurate as a forward-looking flag pre-merge but becomes a stale historical attribution immediately after this PR merges. DISPATCH-NOTE lists 'Closes: ADOPT-001 §12.7.5 forward-looking flag for rule-regression issue template' as a slice commitment but the text of §12.7.5 is not updated. By contrast, §12.7.11 was correctly retitled 'Freshness warning (post-020H.1)' and §12.7.13 retitled 'Supply-chain posture (post-020H.2)' — the landing-signal convention is established.
findings.impact: Post-merge, adopters reading §12.7.5 encounter '(lands in 020H.1)' and must infer it means 'this already happened.' Minor governance doc hygiene issue; no functional impact. Inconsistent with the established §12.7.11 / §12.7.13 landing-signal pattern.
findings.mitigation: Update §12.7.5 step 4 from '(lands in 020H.1)' to '(landed in 020H.1)' or remove the parenthetical entirely. One-word fix; the template is already live so the parenthetical's informational purpose is exhausted.

findings.claim: docs/reviews/rule-proposals/README.md cites D-031 by ID only without the canonical path 'docs/DECISIONS.md', differing from the citation style used throughout the governance corpus.
findings.evidence: README.md §Process §2 'Review window': 'A single approval represents quorum because (a) the SCP estate is single-operator at v1.0.0 (per D-031, with bus-factor-1 escalation review at 2026-07-21).' No path given. VERSIONING.md 'References' section: 'docs/DECISIONS.md D-022 — initial federation primitive adoption.' ADOPT-001 §12.7 References block: 'docs/DECISIONS.md D-022 (federation-primitive adoption); D-029 ...; D-030 ...' — file path included in the lead citation. The governance convention is to include docs/DECISIONS.md in D-NNN citations.
findings.impact: A proposer reading the RFC README for the first time, unfamiliar with the decision corpus structure, cannot directly navigate to D-031. Governance audit trail readability slightly degraded for the primary entry point for rule proposers.
findings.mitigation: Update the D-031 citation in README.md from 'per D-031' to 'per docs/DECISIONS.md D-031'. Symmetric improvement: update RULE-TEMPLATE.md §11 'References' boilerplate from 'Related decisions (docs/DECISIONS.md D-NNN)' if it uses plain 'D-NNN' form — confirm whether the template already uses the full path citation.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE hedges rule-proposal auto-defer GitHub Action as 'file as a tracked-forward item if needed' without resolving whether it is needed, leaving an ambiguous governance disposition that is neither TF-filed nor explicitly rejected.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE 'Out of scope / forward-looking' para 2: 'Rule-proposal auto-defer is currently a manual close + defer label step. A GitHub Action that does this on a schedule is forward-compat — file as a tracked-forward item if needed.' No TF-020H1-NNN entry for auto-defer appears in STATUS.md. Per the no-silent-descope governance invariant, deferred items must be named and tracked or explicitly closed as not needed — 'if needed' is not a governance disposition.
findings.impact: Future slice authors and reviewers scanning STATUS.md cannot determine whether auto-defer was considered necessary and deferred (expect a TF entry) or considered unnecessary and rejected (expect a DISPATCH-NOTE closure statement). The ambiguity creates a gap in the audit trail for a feature that the README explicitly calls out as forward-compatible.
findings.mitigation: Make an explicit determination: (a) if needed — add TF-020H1-003: 'rule-proposal auto-defer GitHub Action — currently manual close + defer label; GitHub Action on schedule for WP-SCP-024 estate cascade; no deadline' to STATUS.md; or (b) if not needed — add a sentence to the DISPATCH-NOTE: 'auto-defer is intentionally manual for v1.0.0 single-operator mode; no TF item filed; reassess at WP-SCP-024 multi-maintainer transition.' No ambiguous 'if needed' middle ground.

findings.claim: TF-020H3-003 (plan doc trailing-dash fix) named 020H.1 as its 'likely' closure slice but 020H.1 does not address it, leaving the TF open without an updated closure-path estimate.
findings.evidence: STATUS.md 'Tracked-forward items from 020H part 3' TF-020H3-003: 'Plan §4 020H part 3 canonical YAML wrapper text uses `standards-control-plane` (no trailing dash) in two places... Closure path: governance-only PR amending the plan doc on the next plan-touch slice (likely 020H.1 planning pass).' The 020H.1 DISPATCH-NOTE makes no mention of TF-020H3-003. The plan doc at docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020H part 3 row still contains 'standards-control-plane' (no trailing dash) in the canonical wrapper YAML. WP-SCP-020 is closed; the plan is frozen; the 'likely 020H.1' attribution is now past.
findings.impact: TF-020H3-003 accumulates as an open item with an expired 'likely 020H.1' pointer. Subsequent slices that don't touch the plan will each see the stale pointer. The item is cosmetic (plan doc vs ADOPT-001 already has the correct trailing dash) but the stale pointer degrades STATUS.md readability.
findings.mitigation: Either (a) apply the one-line plan doc fix in this PR's diff (change 'standards-control-plane' to 'standards-control-plane-' in the two affected places in §4 020H part 3); or (b) update TF-020H3-003 closure path in STATUS.md to note 'plan is now frozen post-WP-SCP-020 closure; cosmetic-only; de-prioritized indefinitely; no future slice will amend the frozen plan' so the pointer is resolved rather than left as 'likely 020H.1'.

findings.claim: RULE-TEMPLATE.md §6 'Conflict-gate strategy' prompts for Python evaluator expressibility and fixture list but omits the SCP-E005 merge-blocking consequence and the adapter contract at tests/conflict_gate/adapter.py, leaving a first-time proposer without operational stakes.
findings.evidence: RULE-TEMPLATE.md §6: 'Are the rule's match conditions expressible in the Python evaluator today? If not, what's the closure path? What conflict-gate fixtures will be added to tests/conflict_gate/?' No mention of: (a) SCP-E005 (the merge-blocking error code emitted on Rego/Python disagreement, per ADOPT-001 §12.7.6: 'Disagreement → SCP-E005 → merge-blocked → amending decision row in a separate PR resolves it'); (b) tests/conflict_gate/adapter.py (the normalization contract both engines run through, per WP-SCP-020 §4 020C.1 iv). A proposer answering 'not expressible in Python' may not understand the operational consequence.
findings.impact: A proposer who does not know the conflict-gate infrastructure may propose a rule whose Python evaluator gap will merge-block PRs until a separate D-NNN adjudication PR lands. The false-positive surface of §6 — specifically, what 'not expressible' means for PR flow — is not communicated.
findings.mitigation: Add one bullet to RULE-TEMPLATE.md §6: 'Note: a rule whose match conditions are not yet expressible in the Python evaluator will emit SCP-E005 (merge-blocked) on any shared fixture where Rego and Python disagree; the unblock path is a separate D-NNN adjudication PR updating tests/conflict_gate/adapter.py and the expected-verdict fixtures (per ADOPT-001 §12.7.6). Name the expected adjudication timeline in the Open questions (§10) if closure is not imminent.'

structured_review.summary: Slice 020H.1 genuinely closes WP-SCP-020 §4 020H.1 sub-criteria (i)–(iv) and the folded-in 020H part 3 sub-criterion (x) freshness-warning. VERSIONING.md, rule-proposals README+RULE-TEMPLATE, rule-regression issue template, canary-replay.yml, version-manifest.json, and policy-check.yml freshness step all materially match the plan spec wording. The 020H.2 STATUS.md carrier-slice backfill is confirmed present (PR #77 commit bac1427). ADOPT-001 §12.7.11 retitled 'post-020H.1' and §12.7.7 SCP-FRESH-001 row are confirmed live. Plan §3 sequence shows WP-SCP-020 closed at Threshold A; no in-flight 020H.1 claim in the plan doc. Pre-commit hook Regal exclusion is correctly surfaced only in ADOPT-001 §12.7.9, not in VERSIONING.md (appropriate — not a public surface). Three MAJ findings and five MIN findings prevent fixpoint. MAJ items: (1) three forward-looking items named in the DISPATCH-NOTE are not filed as TF-020H1-NNN entries in STATUS.md, with one of those tracking claims actively false against VERSIONING.md content; (2) no D-036 ratifying the semver contract and RFC process as new estate doctrine, breaking the D-035/020G pattern.
